_comment: Japanese overrides — human-forced translations for terms and sentences the LLM gets wrong, applied last so they always win over the pipeline's output. hooks/locales/ja.json is pipeline-generated (Task 6 of gate-message-i18n) rather than hand-translated, so this file only gains entries where a specific value was found to be wrong; ja.json ships, this file is what makes the correction survive the next `npm run translate:hooks`. Both must be edited together — tests/hook-locales-ja-meaning.test.js fails if they drift apart. Key -> hooks/locales/zh.json key, mirroring client/src/i18n/ja.override.json's shape.
_comment_meaning: The six entries below are semantic corrections, not phrasing preferences. zh.json writes its safety negations inside emphasis brackets (這個指令「沒有」被把關 / 這一輪「沒有」被檢查) and the pipeline rendered the bracketed 「沒有」 as a noun value — 「なし」でチェックされました — whose final predicate is affirmative completed passive, i.e. it told a Japanese reader the check HAPPENED while en.json says it did NOT. A machine whose OS locale is ja gets Japanese with no opt-in, so these read as an all-clear during a fail-open. Corrected to end on a negative predicate (…チェックされていません); lint.recovered is the mirror case, an affirmative notice the pipeline turned into 検出されました ("something was detected"), which is a different claim from "this turn was checked".
